[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a period of 2 years, the Principal can be calculated directly using the relationship between CI and SI:

Principal (P) = (SI ÷ 2)² ÷ (CI − SI)

⇒ P = (60 ÷ 2)² ÷ (64 − 60)

⇒ P = 30² ÷ 4 = 900 ÷ 4 = 225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹60

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹64

Time (T) = 2 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b0722c52d72712ccb3be7fdcb8ac86ce7f429f542cba5ce53a13cfea16cc65c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 1 year = 60 ÷ 2 = ₹30

⇒ The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is simply the interest generated on the 1st year's SI.

⇒ Difference = CI − SI = 64 − 60 = ₹4

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest on SI × 100) ÷ SI for 1st year

⇒ R = (4 × 100) ÷ 30 = 40/3 %

⇒ Now, substituting the values in the 1-year SI formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 30 = (P × 40/3 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 30 = (P × 40) ÷ 300

⇒ P = (30 × 300) ÷ 40 = 9000 ÷ 40 = 225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The formula is: Difference = P × (R / 100)², which effectively equals the interest earned on the first year's simple interest.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The formula for 3 years is: Difference = P × (R / 100)² × (3 + R / 100).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is charged entirely on the base principal amount, whereas compound interest is charged on the principal as well as any accumulated interest from previous periods (interest on interest).

⇒ 900 ÷ P = 63 - 60

⇒ 900 ÷ P = 3

⇒ P = 900 ÷ 3

⇒ P = ₹300

For **half-yearly compounding**, Rate (R) becomes R/2 and Time (n) becomes 2n.

Effective Rate = 8% ÷ 2 = 4% per half-year.

Time periods = 1 year × 2 = 2 periods.

Effective % for 2 periods = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

Amount = 7500 × 108.16% = 75 × 108.16 = ₹8112.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8112.**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹7,500, **Rate (R)** = 8% p.a., **Time (n)** = 1 year.

⇒ For **compounded half-yearly**, New Rate (r) = 8%/2 = 4%.

⇒ New Time (T) = 1 × 2 = 2 periods.

⇒ A = 7500(1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 7500(1 + 1/25)²

⇒ A = 7500 × (26/25) × (26/25)

⇒ A = 12 × 26 × 26

⇒ A = 12 × 676 = 8112

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8112.**

**__Additional Information__**

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is **compounded quarterly**, the annual rate is divided by 4 and the time is multiplied by 4.

Effective Interest Rate

The **effective rate** for compounding can be calculated using the formula [ (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1 ] × 100.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

Rate (R) = **8% per annum**

Time (n) = **1 year**

Compounding: **Half-yearly**

Amount (A) = P[1 + (r/100)]ⁿ

For quarterly compounding, divide the annual rate by 4 and multiply the time in years by 4. For half-yearly, divide rate by 2 and multiply time by 2.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself on compound interest in 15 years. In what duration will it become 8 times of itself, considering annual compounding?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **T** years, it becomes **nx** times in **x × T** years.

Given: **n = 2** times in **T = 15** years.

We need **8** times, which is **2³** times.

Here, **x = 3**. Therefore, **Required Time = 3 × 15 = 45 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0b89f1d30f26f3e203e84ca4802e7ee9a027bd455f6b872c059ef07f2f25cd8.png] 

**Given:** Sum becomes **2 times** in 15 years.

**Formula:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁵

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁵ --- (Equation 1)

To find time (t) for **8 times** the sum:

⇒ 8P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 8 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 2³ = (1 + r/100)t

Substituting the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁵]³ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁴⁵ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ t = **45 years**

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The formula for annual compounding is A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where A is the amount, P is the principal, r is the rate, and n is the time in years.

Rule of doubling (CI)

In CI, the time taken for a sum to grow from 1 to 2, 2 to 4, 4 to 8, and so on, remains constant for a fixed interest rate.

SI vs CI growth

Simple interest grows **linearly** (constant addition), whereas Compound Interest grows **exponentially** (constant multiplication).</p

questions.question: If a sum of money doubles itself in 10 years on compound interest, then in how many more years will it become 16 times of itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Let the **sum of money** become **2ⁿ** times in **n × T** years, where **T** is the time to **double**.

Here, the **sum doubles** in 10 years, so **T = 10 years**.

We need the sum to become **16 times**, and 16 = 2**⁴**.

Total time for 16 times = **4 × 10 = 40 years**.

**Additional years** required = **40 − 10 = 30 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ca1eb111e9508f4a77abb0a3981260d6ecc03519e3dd590363822f49c1eb162.png] 
**Given:**

Time to double (P → 2P) = **10 years**

Target amount = **16 times (16P)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ For doubling: 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰ ⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ For 16 times: 16P = P(1 + r/100)T ⇒ 16 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (2)⁴ = [(1 + r/100)¹⁰]⁴

⇒ (1 + r/100)T = (1 + r/100)⁴⁰

⇒ Total time (T) = **40 years**

⇒ **More years** needed = Total time − Initial time = 40 − 10 = **30 years**

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Growth

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **x** times in **t** years, it will become **xⁿ** times in **n × t** years.

Simple Interest vs CI Growth

In **Simple Interest**, if a sum doubles (becomes 2P) in 10 years, it means it adds P interest every 10 years. To become 16P, it needs 15P interest, taking 15 × 10 = 150 years.</p
